items.title: What Rising U.S. Yields Mean for Latin America's Borrowing Bill
items.summary: We see the recent surge in U.S. long-term yields as a differentiating force across Latin America rather than a uniform headwind, amplifying pre-existing vulnerabilities in higher-debt sovereigns but leaving resilient credits comparatively insulated. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: We're Downgrading Moderna to Sell/High Risk
items.summary: We’re downgrading Moderna to Sell/High Risk after an outsized run and amid struggles to justify the valuation through public-company comparisons or pipeline net present value. MRNA’s ~$80 billion market cap approximates Regeneron’s despite materially lower expected revenue and earnings.

items.title: Core PCE Is Revised Even Lower Than Expected
items.summary: Core PCE inflation rose 0.25% month over month and 3.01% year over year in August, softer than we'd expected. While still above target, core PCE is now clearly softer than the latest Fed forecasts, which we think will encourage policymakers to "wait and see" before pursuing further hikes.

items.title: U.S. Lodging and REITs: Impacts of an Agentic AI World
items.summary: We consider the potential impacts of agentic AI on real estate fundamentals, as well as trading/macro considerations given that REITs are generally considered “risk off” vs. the broad market. We offer initial thoughts by sector, while staying humble knowing that the technology is evolving.

items.title: The Shape of Boeing's Free Cash Flow Steepens
items.summary: We're lowering our Boeing free cash flow estimates to account for a steepening ramp over the next several years. As we explore in this note, we expect near-term trading to stay data-driven until we have some degree of resolution on recent certification and labor issues at BA.

items.title: Western Europe Airlines: Legacy Airline Competitive Capacity
items.summary: Our competitive overlap analysis for EU legacy airlines shows another month of broad-based cuts to scheduled capacity. While capacity growth remains lower on legacy carriers' networks vs. low-cost carriers, larger cuts for low-cost names show the gap is narrowing.

items.title: Western Europe Aerospace & Defense: EU Spending Hints
items.summary: The European Council has identified five "European Defence Projects of Common Interest." We offer our analysis of potential implications in this note, including the observation that traditional defense should continue to dominate spending and air defense seems to be the main priority.

items.title: North America Specialty Chemicals: Trimming Coatings Estimates
items.summary: Coatings companies have seen relative weakness in September given higher oil prices, rate hikes and continued weakness in housing, autos and Europe. We trim EPS estimates ~2% for the rest of the year and 2027. We see price/cost expansion as likely significant in next year's second half.

items.title: India Economics: El Niño Risks Are Still Unfolding
items.summary: India's macro risks are rising as the monsoon nears its end, with rainfall deficits in key agricultural states possibly threatening yields. The focus will shift to tracking elevated daily temperatures as heat-wave risks are heightened during the March-April harvest period.

items.title: What to Expect from Brazil’s Elections
items.summary: Brazil will elect a new president, 27 state governors, two-thirds of the Senate and all the Lower House members on Oct. 4. We see expect monetary policy to be on hold, reduce our GDP growth forecast for next year, and consider further likely impacts of the elections in this note.

items.title: Australia Raises Rates, With Further Hikes Expected
items.summary: Australia delivered a fourth 25-basis-point hike this year in a unanimous and decidedly hawkish decision that came despite an easing in housing activity, signaling a clear focus on inflation over the labor market. We see November as the sweet spot for another 25-bp hike.

items.title: Why Aren't U.S. Utilities Building Large Nuclear Plants?
items.summary: We're often asked why U.S. utilities aren't building large nuclear plants and believe announcing such a project would hurt share prices. The answer is a combination of risks, including construction cost overruns, data-center politics, wariness of "big bets" and not wanting to go first.

items.title: China Economics: A Coordinated Fiscal-Monetary  Push
items.summary: The People's Bank of China announced a cut to the PSL rate, expanding its usage and relending tools, and the long-awaited mortgage interest subsidy program was also confirmed. The policy focus is likely to remain on investment this year, with a pivot toward domestic demand yet to emerge.

items.title: Saudi Arabia Economics: A Look Back, a Look Ahead
items.summary: We take stock of the first half of the year for Saudi Arabia and look ahead. The economy has tipped into recession, with second-quarter GDP contracting 4.8% quarter on quarter. Looking ahead, we consider three scenarios and discuss implications for the country's macro outlook.

items.title: Equity Markets Positioning Model: A Polarized Landscape
items.summary: The dominant positioning story remains one of increasing concentration and not broad-based risk taking. Across U.S. indices, risk flows continue to skew toward large caps while small caps remain heavily bearish, leaving positioning increasingly one-sided. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Global Commodities: Fourth-Quarter Outlook
items.summary: Our fourth-quarter commodities outlook includes an in-depth look at the global diesel market. A normalization of Strait of Hormuz flows by year's end would create a bullish environment for metals. We see upside risks for agricultural prices given ongoing and potential supply shocks.

items.title: SIGN (Sector & Industry Group Navigator): Navigating Uncertainty
items.summary: Our third-quarter broadening call was working well until Jackson Hole, when interest rate/inflation headwinds, along with oil price pressures, combined to flip the playbook. Given persistent macro and AI uncertainties, our fourth-quarter positioning response is best described as eclectic.

items.title: Permian Gas Growth: The Path to Reclaiming the Natural Gas Crown
items.summary: We see the Permian at an inflection point, with the basin poised to become the largest U.S. gas producer, complementing its oil crown. But fully utilizing capacity will require flexing all levers simultaneously. We explore what's needed and offer more analysis in this note.

items.title: U.S.-China Summit Preserves Stability Amid Practical Deliverables
items.summary: The U.S.-China summit delivered on optics, reaffirming “strategic stability" and raising the possibility of more 2026 Trump-Xi meetings. As expected, deliverables were modest but practical, including a two-month trade truce extension, a $30 billion tariff reduction, and a new AI dialogue.

items.title: European Auto Manufacturers: Autos, Investors and Good Dreams
items.summary: Ray Dalio once said "investors are buying dreams, not earnings." Unfortunately, most European auto OEMs are providing bad dreams, and the sector needs to start delivering good ones for investors to return. Porsche has started to do that and been rewarded. Can other OEMs follow its lead?

items.title: U.S. Communications Equipment: OCS Is an $11 Billion Opportunity
items.summary: Optical circuit switching is turning into a multi-year trend in AI Optics. We debut our OCS TAM Model, which indicates OCS could be an $11 billion opportunity for vendors such as COHR and LITE. We revise our estimates for LITE and raise our target price to $1,400.

items.title: Could Minor Changes Drive a Mexico Market Bounce?
items.summary: Mixed economic signals are keeping Mexico's growth outlook modest, but a slower fiscal consolidation path is increasing risks to the country's investment-grade status. Mexican assets face primarily external pressures; we trim our S&P IPC targets to 68,000 for 2026 and 72,000 for mid-2027.

items.title: Africa Economics & Strategy Weekly: What's Ahead for Egypt?
items.summary: We discuss key themes we expect from a new Egyptian policy document set for release in the coming months. Then we look at Egypt's current inflation dynamics and what they imply for the inflation's path and the dynamics of 2027 monetary policy.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: Neutrals Are Back in Style for Fall
items.summary: There's still little reason for investors to get overweight duration here now that the Fed has opened the upside risks of the distribution. We look at ’99 and ‘23 to conclude that a selloff above 5.5% in 10y yields is unlikely. But UST investors may have a better backdrop into 2027.

items.title: U.S. Economics Weekly: A More Hawkish Reaction Function
items.summary: A reaction function that includes energy prices means risks skew hawkish in the near-term. But we see underlying inflation cooling and our base case is for the Fed to pursue significantly less hawkish policy than what's currently priced by the market. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Emerging Markets Economic Outlook & Strategy: A Higher-Yielding World
items.summary: The reasons for core (U.S.) rising yields matter. We believe we're entering a more adverse regime for emerging markets, with heightened supply-side inflation shocks and a more hawkish Fed likely putting net commodity-importing EM under pressure. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Global Asset Allocation: Rates Bite, Equities Fight
items.summary: Since our last asset allocation, we've seen a triple punch against global duration, driven by hawkish front-end repricing from the Fed, ECB, and the Bank of England in conjunction with higher oil prices. We offer further analysis in this note and explore strategies in response.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Mixed Signals
items.summary: We expect the third quarter to be another solid reporting period, though management commentary will likely be somewhat cautionary headed into year's end, given multiple headwinds. We continue to focus on oil prices as key to the macro backdrop as we navigate the post-Jackson Hole pivot.

items.title: European Ingredients: Cooking with Capital
items.summary: In this Deep Dive, we use a returns lens to reassess franchise quality and conclude that ingredients stocks remain a high-quality peer group whose compounder characteristics should reassert themselves as growth returns. We upgrade Kerry to Buy, seeing it as fundamentally undervalued.

items.title: We're Upgrading Komatsu to Buy
items.summary: We're upgrading Komatsu to Buy. We expect solid first-half results, led by strength in mining equipment. We model sales of ¥1.1 trillion (+13% year over year) and above-consensus operating profit of ¥155 billion. The recent share price correction means ETR exceeds 15%.

items.title: We See Sustainable Double-Digit EPS Growth for Trane
items.summary: We think Trane has a favorable setup for sustained double-digit EPS growth. Data-center investment should extend CHVAC’s growth runway, while the breadth of TT’s end-market exposure could provide additional upside potential as residential HVAC and transport markets improve over time.

items.title: U.S. Rates Strategy: Tell-Tail Signs?
items.summary: Thursday’s rout in the Treasury market roughly peaked after the second-worst 5y auction tail over the past 15 years. However, the 7y auction finds itself in the crosshairs of a hawkish Fed backdrop, combined with the Treasury market challenging Secretary Bessent’s long-end “put.”

items.title: U.S. Demographic Trends Provide Support for BEVs
items.summary: We look at buying trends of Millennials and Gen Z, with an eye on People Carriers and electrified vehicles. Survey results from our Innovation Lab reinforce our case that these trends will boost U.S. market penetration for both categories, with GM, Ford, Lucid and Rivian names of note.

items.title: Global Artificial Intelligence: The Efficiency Dividend
items.summary: The latest frontier models' gains in performance and cost per task highlight improving model efficiency and inference economics, potentially reinforcing a longer-term economic advantage over open-weight alternatives. Trends we observe should amplify the value of routing and orchestration.

items.title: Global Economic Outlook & Strategy: Sunshine Despite Cloudy Skies
items.summary: Our “global resilience” narrative remains firmly intact, as the global economy's production side has grown more flexible and adaptable and AI spending has emerged as a robust engine of growth. Our 2026 global-growth forecast is now tracking at 2.6%, and we see it firming next year to 2.8%.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: Headwinds Are Getting Stronger
items.summary: Emerging markets have demonstrated remarkable resilience during the energy crisis, but with central banks entering the final innings of their rate-cutting cycles, recent supportive tailwinds are beginning to fade as inflation pressures build with the energy backdrop.

items.title: European Rates Weekly: Higher Yields Are Here to Stay
items.summary: Near-term risks skew bearish, but our new forecasts look for 10yr Bund yields to settle below spot at 3.4% for the medium term. OAT volatility could be a limiting factor for ECB hikes (and therefore the Bund sell-off). We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: The Speculative Grade Beat: AI’s Record-Setting High-Yield Entrance
items.summary: The high-yield market just absorbed its largest-ever deal, $10 billion from SoftBank to fund its stake in a frontier AI lab. This transaction introduces a new form of AI development risk into a universe dominated by asset-heavy data centers. We discuss the implications in this note.

items.title: Mexico Economics: No Need to Follow the Fed Now
items.summary: Banxico left rates unchanged and dropped its explicit guidance that such a course was appropriate, instead emphasizing that future decisions will depend on the disinflation process and its determinants. It also stated that monetary policy need not react mechanically to expected Fed moves.

items.title: Foreign Exchange Forecasts: September 2026
items.summary: We flip bullish USD following a more hawkish-than-expected Fed and with our base case of U.S.-Iran re-escalation materializing. We think U.S. capital flow dynamics remain supportive for USD amid AI tailwinds, attractive real rates, and rising EUR-centric risk premia.

items.title: What Are the Upstream Implications of Action on Diesel?
items.summary: Amid apparent political momentum for a diesel ban/quota, alternative approaches are now reportedly being considered, including voluntary cuts. We look at the "ban playbook" and why it would likely continue, as well as the potential impacts of voluntary cuts.

items.title: Meta Connect ‘26: Muse Is at the Center of Meta’s AI Vision
items.summary: Meta Connect saw Meta's AI product strategy comes into view across Muse, its models and newer devices. Muse is emerging as the centerpiece of Meta’s strategic approach, expanding use cases as downloads, adoption and usage trends continue to significantly outperform expectations.

items.title: We're Upgrading MTU Aero Engines to Buy
items.summary: We're upgrading MTU Aero Engines to Buy from Sell. While MTU's 30% EV/EBIT discount to Safran has been an accurate reflection of its position for some time, we think this backdrop is now changing, with MTU's robust EBIT outlook justifying a narrowing of the multiple between it and Safran.

items.title: Standing at the Crossroads of Healthcare and AI
items.summary: AI has become pervasive across healthcare, part of everything from clinical-trial design and R&D investment to hospital information systems. In this Super-Sector Analysis, we offer a high-level exploration of the intersection of AI and healthcare as we turn the page to 2027 and beyond.
